testName: Class A Knowledge Test #2 50 Questions • Passing Score 40

questions.question: If you are not sure if your vehicle can safely fit under a bridge, you should:
questions.explanation: If you are not sure your vehicle will fit under a bridge, slow down and find another route if possible.

questions.question: What can change the height of a vehicle?
questions.explanation: Heavy cargo makes a vehicle sit lower. A light vehicle is taller than the same vehicle carrying a heavy load. If your vehicle fits under a bridge when full, it may not fit when empty.

questions.question: An air compressor governor stops pumping air when the tanks reach:
questions.explanation: The air compressor governor stops pumping when air pressure reaches 125 psi. This is called the "cut-out" level.

questions.question: How much water must be on a road for a vehicle to hydroplane?

options.text: A good amount, such as a large puddle

questions.explanation: Hydroplaning happens when your tires lose grip and slide on water. Only a small amount of water is needed for this to happen.

questions.question: What color is the low air pressure warning light?
questions.explanation: The low air pressure warning light is red. It may also have a buzzer sound.

questions.question: Texting while driving is especially dangerous because:

options.text: It is both a mental and physical distraction.
A message may upset the driver.
People like to read and may become too focused on their phones.

questions.correctAnswerText: It is both a mental and physical distraction.
questions.explanation: Texting is dangerous because it takes your mind off driving and requires you to take at least one hand off the wheel.

questions.question: Talking on a hands-free phone while driving:

options.text: Only distracts the driver if the driver is speaking.

questions.explanation: Hands-free phones are safer than hand-held phones, but conversations still take your mental focus away from driving.

questions.question: In very hot weather, air pressure in tires may decrease.
questions.explanation: Hot air expands, so tire pressure increases in hot weather. Stop often to check your tires and prevent blowouts.

questions.question: If equipped, a header board should:

options.text: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
Light up when the engine starts.

questions.correctAnswerText: Be strong enough to hold cargo.
questions.explanation: A header board must be secure, undamaged, and strong enough to keep cargo from falling.

questions.question: A ____ between the air compressor and tank prevents air from escaping if the compressor leaks.
questions.explanation: A one-way check valve is placed between the air compressor and main tank. It stops air from leaking back if the compressor breaks.

questions.question: What should you do if an oncoming driver has their high beam headlights on?

options.text: Flash your high beam lights to signal the driver to use low beams.
Look toward the right side of your lane until the vehicle passes.
Pull to the side of the road until the vehicle passes.

questions.correctAnswerText: Look toward the right side of your lane until the vehicle passes.
questions.explanation: When an oncoming vehicle uses high beam headlights, look away from the lights toward the right edge of the road until it passes. This prevents you from being blinded.

questions.question: Are tires with deep cracks acceptable?
questions.explanation: Tires must be checked for damage. Deep cracks are not acceptable.

questions.question: For a 40-foot load, what is the minimum number of tie-downs needed?
questions.explanation: Cargo on flatbed trailers must be tied down with at least one tie-down for every 10 feet of cargo. A minimum of two tie-downs must always be used, regardless of cargo size.

questions.question: What should drivers do with a front brake limiting valve to maintain normal stopping power?

options.text: Keep it at the halfway point.

questions.explanation: Some older vehicles have a front brake limiting valve with "normal" and "slippery" settings. Keep this valve in the "normal" position for proper braking power.

questions.question: Why should a driver accelerate slowly when traction is poor?

options.text: Because slow acceleration is always best.
To avoid losing control of the vehicle.
To stay behind the vehicle ahead.
To be the last vehicle through an intersection.

questions.correctAnswerText: To avoid losing control of the vehicle.
questions.explanation: Quick acceleration on slippery roads causes loss of control. Accelerate smoothly and gradually when traction is poor.

questions.question: Is using a helper when backing up recommended?
questions.explanation: Use a helper when backing up. The helper should watch blind spots and stand where the driver can see them.

questions.question: At 55 mph under ideal conditions, how far does an air brake vehicle need to stop completely?
questions.explanation: Stopping distance includes perception time, reaction time, brake lag, and braking distance. An air brake vehicle traveling 55 mph needs about 450 feet to stop completely under ideal conditions.

questions.question: If your vehicle catches fire, what should you NOT do?

options.text: Park away from buildings, trees, brush, and other vehicles.
Call emergency services and report your location.

questions.explanation: If your vehicle is on fire, leave the road and stop in an open area. Do not go to a service station because fuel there could catch fire. Call emergency services right away.

questions.question: When should you check and adjust your mirrors?
questions.explanation: Check and adjust your mirrors before you start driving. Your position changes day to day, so mirrors may need adjustment.

questions.question: To avoid hitting a hazard on the road, what may be safer?

options.text: You should always try to stop.
Swerving may be safer than stopping.

questions.correctAnswerText: Swerving may be safer than stopping.
questions.explanation: Swerving around a hazard is sometimes safer than braking hard. You can usually turn away from something faster than you can stop.

questions.question: When driving down a hill, a vehicle's speed will likely:
questions.explanation: Gravity pulls a vehicle faster when driving downhill, so speed increases.

questions.question: When turning, when should you turn off the turn signal?
questions.explanation: Keep your signal on the whole time you are turning. Turn it off only after you finish the turn.

questions.question: Blocking cargo:

options.text: Should be done to stop cargo from moving.
Can only be done with metal pieces.

questions.correctAnswerText: Should be done to stop cargo from moving.
questions.explanation: Blocking and bracing keep cargo from shifting while driving. Block cargo on the front, back, and sides to prevent it from moving.

questions.question: After changing a tire, you should drive a short distance and then stop to:

options.text: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
See if rocks are in the tread.

questions.correctAnswerText: Check that the lug nuts are tight.
questions.explanation: After you start driving with a new tire, stop after a short distance and check that the lug nuts are tight.

questions.question: With a manual transmission, you can stop your vehicle from rolling backward when starting by:

options.text: Slightly engage the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake.
Put the vehicle in reverse before moving forward.
Fully engage the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake.
Put the vehicle in neutral before moving forward.

questions.correctAnswerText: Slightly engage the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake.
questions.explanation: To stop rolling backward when starting on a hill, slightly engage the clutch before lifting your foot off the brake. Use the parking brake if needed to prevent rolling back.

questions.question: If vehicles are having trouble passing your truck on a road with two or more lanes, you should:
questions.explanation: Stay in the right lane when your truck is going slower due to a heavy load. This lets other vehicles pass you in the left lane.

questions.question: At speeds under 40 mph, keep at least ____ of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length.
questions.explanation: At speeds under 40 mph, allow one second of following distance for every 10 feet of your vehicle's length. At faster speeds, add at least one more second.

questions.question: When air pressure drops to between ____, a low pressure warning should activate.
questions.explanation: A low pressure warning light, buzzer, or wig wag should activate before air pressure drops to between 55 and 75 psi.

questions.question: Vehicle inspections are required:
questions.explanation: Federal and state laws require drivers to inspect their vehicles before every trip.

questions.question: When brakes create too much heat:
questions.explanation: If brakes get too hot, they may fade and lose their ability to slow the vehicle. Do not rely only on brakes. Also use engine braking to slow down.

questions.question: During a basic vehicle control skills test, what is a look?

options.text: A driver checks the gauges on the dashboard.
A driver checks their blind spots.
A driver gets out and walks to the back of the vehicle to check where it is.

questions.correctAnswerText: A driver gets out and walks to the back of the vehicle to check where it is.
questions.explanation: A look happens when a driver gets out of their seat, leaves the vehicle, and walks to the back to check its position. During straight line backing, you can use only one look. During other exercises, you can use up to two looks.

questions.question: What is the maximum safe air leakage rate for a double combination vehicle during a static leakage test?
questions.explanation: For a double combination vehicle with air brakes, the air should leak no more than 3 psi in one minute. If air leaks faster than this, the vehicle should not be driven. Something needs to be repaired.

questions.question: Transporting hanging meat in a refrigerated truck:

options.text: Is a good way for new drivers to gain experience.

questions.explanation: A skilled driver is needed to transport hanging meat. This cargo is unstable because it has a high center of gravity and the swinging meat can affect how the driver controls the vehicle.

questions.question: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the highest safe level, you should:

options.text: Pull over and find out what is wrong.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull over and find out what is wrong.
questions.explanation: If the coolant temperature gauge goes above the highest safe level, stop driving right away and check the problem. There may be an issue that could cause engine failure or a fire.

questions.question: During the driving test, the examiner will score you on:

options.text: How fast you reach your destination.

questions.explanation: The examiner will score you on specific driving moves and your overall driving behavior. You must drive safely, obey all traffic signs and laws, and not cause accidents or traffic violations.

questions.question: If you see lights ahead while driving in fog:

options.text: You can assume the lights are on the road.
The lights may be a reflection.
The lights may be an optical illusion.
The lights may not show where the road is. The vehicle may have left the roadway.

questions.correctAnswerText: The lights may not show where the road is. The vehicle may have left the roadway.
questions.explanation: In fog, lights are not a reliable guide to where the road is. The lights could come from a vehicle that has driven off the road.

questions.question: Which of the following is NOT a warning sign of fatigue?
questions.explanation: Warning signs of fatigue include trouble focusing, frequent blinking, heavy eyelids, repeated yawning, rubbing your eyes, daydreaming, trouble remembering recent miles, missing exits or signs, trouble keeping your head up, drifting from your lane, following too closely, hitting rumble strips, and feeling restless or irritable.

questions.question: Most heavy trucks with manual transmissions require ____ to change gears.
questions.explanation: Most heavy vehicles with manual transmissions require double clutching to shift gears. You need practice to learn this skill.

questions.question: Sending text messages while driving:

options.text: Is allowed if the messages are short.
Is allowed if you are asking your employer a question.

questions.explanation: Sending and reading text messages while driving is not permitted.

questions.question: If a vehicle has power steering, you should inspect:
questions.explanation: Check the hoses, pumps, and fluid level in a power steering system. Look for leaks in the hoses.

questions.question: When should mirrors be adjusted?

options.text: When you are standing next to the vehicle.

questions.explanation: Check mirrors before you start driving. On vehicles with trailers, you can only adjust mirrors correctly when the trailer is straight.

questions.question: How should you do an offset back/left parking maneuver?

options.text: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
Drive straight back, then pull forward to the left.
Pull straight forward, then drive straight back.

questions.correctAnswerText: Pull straight forward, then back to the left.
questions.explanation: For an offset back/left parking maneuver, first pull straight forward. Then back up to the left. Your vehicle must stay completely within the parking space.

questions.question: What should you do if you feel tired while driving?

options.text: Drive faster to finish the trip sooner.

questions.explanation: If you feel drowsy, safely pull off the road and sleep. Artificial stimulants like coffee are dangerous because you may crash when they wear off.

questions.question: When entering traffic, which statement is NOT correct?

options.text: Wait for a large gap between vehicles.
Be ready for slow acceleration, especially if your vehicle is loaded.
Make sure you can cross traffic completely without blocking other vehicles.
Assume other drivers will make room for your large vehicle.

questions.correctAnswerText: Assume other drivers will make room for your large vehicle.
questions.explanation: Know your vehicle's size and how long it takes to accelerate. Wait for a gap in traffic large enough for your vehicle. If your vehicle is heavily loaded, it needs even more room. Always make sure you can cross traffic without getting in the way.

questions.question: How often must you check that cargo is secured?
questions.explanation: Check cargo before you start. Check it again within the first 50 miles. After that, check it every 3 hours or every 150 miles.

questions.question: Why can parked delivery trucks be dangerous?

options.text: Drivers or workers are often in a hurry and may not look for traffic before leaving the truck.
Packages often fall out of the trucks onto the road.

questions.correctAnswerText: Drivers or workers are often in a hurry and may not look for traffic before leaving the truck.
questions.explanation: Parked delivery trucks are dangerous because the driver or worker may pull into traffic suddenly or step out without checking for other vehicles.

questions.question: Which of the following does NOT help prevent aggressive driving?

options.text: Not expecting delays on a drive
Keeping a safe distance behind other vehicles
Keeping your hands on the wheel
Not making gestures at other drivers

questions.correctAnswerText: Not expecting delays on a drive
questions.explanation: To avoid aggressive driving, expect delays and plan your travel time realistically. Drive at the right speed, keep a safe distance, do not gesture at other drivers, and keep both hands on the wheel.

questions.question: What is the purpose of tie-downs?
questions.explanation: Tie-downs secure cargo on flatbed trailers and in closed vans. They prevent cargo from shifting or falling while driving. Moving cargo can affect how your vehicle handles.

questions.question: What should you do before driving downhill?

options.text: Take your vehicle out of gear.

questions.explanation: Shift into a lower gear before going downhill. This helps you avoid using your brakes too much.

questions.question: What is true about distracted driving?

options.text: It only happens when drivers physically do something, like use a cell phone.
It can happen when your mind is not focused, like when daydreaming.
It is safe on uncrowded roads.

questions.correctAnswerText: It can happen when your mind is not focused, like when daydreaming.
questions.explanation: Mental distractions are as dangerous as physical ones. You can look at a hazard but miss it if your mind is thinking about something else.
